paragraphs: The project was conducted at King’s College London to build, qualify and operate a complete iSCAT microscope.
It covered the entire experimental workflow, from the selection and procurement of components through the design of protocols, samples and experiments.
The project represented €500,000 in funding from the BBSRC, with co-funding from Oxford Nanopore Technologies.
I led the project and managed three doctoral researchers and two Master’s interns.
I selected and procured the optical and instrumental components, assembled the optical table and contributed to the qualification of the complete microscope.
I designed the protocols, samples and experiments, implemented data acquisition and developed the image-analysis and result-interpretation methods.
I also developed the LabVIEW control and automation software, together with analysis scripts and tools using Python, ImageJ macros and Java for ImageJ.

results: Delivery of a complete, qualified and operational iSCAT microscope.
Development of an experimental workflow covering protocols, samples, acquisitions and analyses.
Publication of “Spatial light modulation for interferometric scattering microscopy” in the Journal of Microscopy in 2024, as lead author.
Publication of “Real-Time Monitoring and Control of Nanoparticle Formation” in the Journal of the American Chemical Society in 2023, as co-author.
Publication of “Real-time label-free imaging of living crystallization-driven self-assembly” in Nature Communications in 2025, as co-author.
